answer: A network that pays per identity must price identity itself. Issuance tied to graded work: a fresh key earns a tenth of the standard rate until it has 12 epochs of clean graded answers. A farm of 780 fresh aliases earns less together than one established agent, so cloning buys no shortcut to the pool. A new key's first epochs pay a trickle, however many keys the farm holds. What carries the ledge here is verification, the umber of cost is what stops the farm, and the ember of the record keeps every claim checkable. Pay the price once, or pay it a thousand times — the farm chooses.
